reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the cited text supports it: the only 'shall not' covenants in the quoted paragraphs are exclusivity/competition restrictions (p0037, p0042) and the independent-contractor/no-joint-venture clause (p0061, where 'employee' is merely a relationship descriptor). None restricts solicitation, hiring, or inducement of either party's personnel, so the preferred position ('No non-solicit on Customer') is already satisfied.

Correctly no redline and no comment for a compliant finding; rendered paragraphs are byte-identical to the originals, which is the right outcome — adding a carve-out or duration cap would require first drafting a restrictive covenant that does not exist and would worsen our position.

The two failed deterministic checks (12-month duration, general-solicitation carve-out) are non-probative here because both test attributes that can only exist inside a non-solicit clause; their failure is consistent with absence rather than a defect in the proposal.
Party mapping is correct: the Company (our client, a 'Company' alias) is the customer and HDI is the vendor/host, so the rule's focus on covenants binding Customer is properly applied.

The out-of-scope note flagging the term-only exclusivity at p0037 versus HDI's term-plus-two-years covenant at p0042 is accurate and appropriately deferred to the exclusivity/non-compete rule rather than shoehorned into NOSOLICIT.
